newsitem.title: USA: FOCUS--Crude draw in API's bullish at first glance.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS--Crude draw in API's bullish at first glance.

text.p: This week's inventory data from the American Petroleum Institute (API) was bullish if the big and unexpected drop in crude stocks was to be believed, traders said.
"It's hard to believe, but I'm still saying it's bullish," said Tom Bentz, analyst with ING Derivatives Clearing, noting the unexpected draw in gasoline stocks was bullish as well.
"That's a stupid number," said one trader referring to the 7.6 million barrel drop in crude stocks last week that brought inventories to 297.8 million or 5.2 million over a year ago.
That crude drop was related mostly to a 5.1 million barrel decline on the U.S. Gulf Coast and a 3.5 million drop on the U.S. West Coast, API said.

Many traders were not satisfied the number was legitimate, noting the API published an equally unbelievable build in Gulf Coast stocks two weeks ago, and chose therefore to interpret the API report as a rather neutral event incapable of stoking oil markets back into an uptrend.
Still, oil prices on ACCESS were heading up after the report, with April crude up 20 cents to $20.86 a barrel, and April gasoline up by 0.50 cents to about 63.40 cents a gallon.

Traders noted the gasoline drop of 1.3 million barrels, which brought total stocks to 201.8 million, was clearly more believable than the crude, adding the the implied demand number of 7.92 million barrels per day was quite bullish.
"It's a confirmation of last week. It's pretty bullish. 7.9 million at this time of year is a good number," said Bob MacMinn, a trader at MPAS Inc in Toronto.

But some worried that the bullish news on the gasoline front was coming a little early and in the midst of a two month downtrend in crude prices, which may hamper gasoline's ability to lead the market into an uptrend.

The API said stocks of heating oil and low sulphur diesel both rose, fueling a 603,000 barrel rise in inventories that looked bearish, but was dismissed by most traders who said the heating oil season is over due to a mild winter.
"Heating is irrelevant and so is gasoline because it's much too early," said another trader.
Runs meanwhile dipped a touch by 0.2 of a percentage point to 88.6 percent of capacity, suggesting the winter refinery maintenance season is still underway.
Until we get some news that changes the market's views, I don't think much will change," said another trader.
"I think the market will be rangebound for the next four to five weeks," he said.
